Package org.geysermc.paletter.block

Class BlockRegistry

java.lang.Object
org.geysermc.paletter.block.BlockRegistry
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.cloudburstmc.protocol.common.DefinitionRegistry<org.cloudburstmc.protocol.bedrock.data.definitions.BlockDefinition>
public final class BlockRegistry extends Object implements org.cloudburstmc.protocol.common.DefinitionRegistry<org.cloudburstmc.protocol.bedrock.data.definitions.BlockDefinition>
The compiled block palette of one Palette: vanilla states plus custom blocks of all layers, with runtime ids assigned the way the client does. It is the block DefinitionRegistry for the codec.

Consumers map against the newest Bedrock version, either by state (resolve(NbtMap)) or, on hot paths, by canonical id (runtimeId(int), block(int): array lookups, see CanonicalBlocks). Differences to older versions (renamed or missing blocks, added or removed states) are handled here.

Runtime ids depend on the palette's BlockNetworkIds mode: palette positions, or state hashes. Each state also has a dense position, indexOf(org.cloudburstmc.protocol.bedrock.data.definitions.BlockDefinition), in both modes; in hashed palettes vanilla definitions are shared between versions.

Since:
1.0.0

    • resolve

      @Internal public @NonNull BlockResolution resolve(@NonNull org.cloudburstmc.nbt.NbtMap state)
      Resolves a block state that is valid in the newest Bedrock version against this palette's version:
      1. an exact match is used as is;
      2. a block that does not exist (or is forcibly replaced, e.g. because it is experimental) is replaced by its fallback;
      3. state values are carried over where the (replacement) block has them; missing or invalid ones use the block's default state values.
      Results are cached. On hot paths, prefer canonical ids (block(int)).
